newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Former security tsar sees "hot autumn" in Russia.
newsitem.headline: Former security tsar sees "hot autumn" in Russia.

text.p: Former security tsar Alexander Lebed, sacked by President Boris Yeltsin on Thursday, predicted that a severe lack of funding for the armed forces would provoke a crisis later this year.

"We are heading for a very hot autumn, no doubt about it," Lebed told a news conference. He cited a letter from a group of General Staff officers in which they told the Defence Ministry to pay all salary arrears by October 25 or face the consequences.

The letter -- published by the Nezavisimaya Gazeta newspaper on Thursday -- was addressed to Defence Minister Igor Rodionov and said that keeping the armed forces "half-starved" was a deliberate act by unnamed sinister forces who wanted to ruin Russia and surrender it to the West.
"We have enough force to make these gentlemen abandon their plans," the letter said. The newspaper did not say how many officers had signed it.
"I think this (crisis) will start on October 25, as can be seen from the letter," Lebed said.

Earlier on Thursday a Yeltsin spokesman hinted that Lebed had been stoking discontent among officers in the paratroop forces, which are due to be reduced under plans for military reform. Yeltsin sacked a deputy paratroop commander for openly protesting against the reforms.
